item.title: Iran says Khamenei had minor injuries but remains out of public view
item.description:
For the first time since the war began, Iran has publicly acknowledged and detailed the injuries sustained by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei during the February 28 US-Israeli strikes that killed his father, former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Mazaher Hosseini, the head of protocol in the office of the supreme leader, said on Friday that Khamenei suffered injuries to his kneecap, lower back, and was struck by a small piece of shrapnel behind his ear during the attack on the supreme leader's compound in central Tehran, according to The Wall Street Journal and Iran International. "During the attack Khamenei was not in the place where the attack took place. They hit his home where his wife was killed. He was on his way, on the stairs, when the missile struck there," Hosseini told supporters in a video shared by Nour News, a media outlet affiliated with Iran's Supreme National Security Council.

Hosseini insisted the 56-year-old cleric is now "in complete health" and said his absence from public life is purely a security precaution. "The enemy is spreading all kinds of rumours and false claims. They want to see him and find him, but people should be patient and not rush. He will speak to you when the time is right," he added.

item.title: Israel built secret base in Iraq during Iran war, WSJ reports
item.description:
Israel established a clandestine military outpost in Iraq's western desert to support its air campaign against Iran and launched airstrikes against Iraqi troops who nearly discovered the site, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter including senior U.S. officials.

The facility was constructed shortly before Operation Roaring Lion began in late February, with the knowledge of the United States but without the approval of Iraq's government. It housed Israeli air force special forces and served as a logistical hub, positioning search-and-rescue teams closer to the Iranian battlefield, roughly 1,000 miles from Israel.

item.title: Global oil stockpiles draining at record pace amid Iran war
item.description: More than two months after the United States and Israel launched coordinated strikes against Iran, the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz is draining the world's oil reserves at a record pace, sending American gasoline prices soaring and threatening European airlines with fuel rationing by summer.

item.title: One Nation wins first federal lower house seat in Farrer by-election
item.description:
Pauline Hanson's One Nation party secured its first-ever seat in the Australian House of Representatives on Saturday, ending the Coalition's 77-year hold on the New South Wales electorate of Farrer in a result that reshapes the country's political landscape.

Candidate David Farley claimed an emphatic victory, leading by roughly 14,000 ballots with more than 80 percent of votes counted. His primary vote hovered around the low 40s on election night, while independent challenger Michelle Milthorpe trailed with approximately a quarter of first preferences. Liberal and National candidates each polled just above 9 percent.

item.title: Iran sends response to US peace proposal via Pakistan after days of delay
item.description:
Iran has submitted its response to the latest US peace proposal through Pakistani mediators, Iranian state media IRNA reported on Sunday, ending days of anticipation as Washington pressed for a reply that Tehran repeatedly withheld.

The submission comes after President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both said last week that a response was expected imminently — only for Iran to keep Washington waiting for four consecutive days. As recently as Saturday, there was no indication that Tehran had delivered its answer, with Trump telling a French broadcaster he still expected to hear back "very soon."

item.title: Iran's record internet blackout threatens mass layoffs as economic toll mounts
item.description: Iran's economy is reeling from the combined effects of war, a record-long internet blackout, and an intensifying U.S. sanctions campaign, with mass layoffs sweeping across industries from petrochemicals to the tech sector and threatening the livelihoods of millions.

item.title: Hantavirus-stricken cruise ship MV Hondius docks at Tenerife
item.description: A Dutch ornithologist's birdwatching trip to the "end of the world" has been traced as the origin of a deadly hantavirus outbreak that has killed three people and infected at least eight aboard and from the expedition cruise ship MV Hondius, which arrived off the coast of Tenerife early Sunday morning carrying more than 140 passengers and crew.

item.title: Netanyahu says Iran war 'not over,' demands uranium removal
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared in an interview airing Sunday on CBS's "60 Minutes" that the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran is "not over," warning that highly enriched uranium still present in Iran must be physically removed and the country's enrichment facilities dismantled before the conflict can be considered resolved.

item.title: Trump set to travel to Beijing for high-stakes Xi summit
item.description:
President Donald Trump is set to travel to Beijing on May 14–15 for a two-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, marking the first U.S. presidential visit to China in nearly nine years and a meeting that will test the fragile détente between the world's two largest economies.

The visit, originally scheduled for late March, was postponed as the United States became embroiled in the war involving Iran and the Israeli-allied campaign that has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Trump confirmed last week that the trip would proceed as planned, telling reporters he expects an "amazing" meeting with his Chinese counterpart.

item.title: Trump accuses Iran of 'playing games,' threatens action
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Sunday accused Iran of "playing games" with the United States, escalating rhetoric as Washington awaits a formal Iranian response to a peace proposal that could end months of conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump warned that Iran would "be made to stop," following days of tense exchanges in the strait and diplomatic back-and-forth mediated by Pakistan. The president also signaled he may resume "Project Freedom Plus" — an expanded version of the military operation to escort commercial vessels through the waterway — if negotiations collapse.

item.title: Iran threatens 'decisive' response to UK, French warships near Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi warned on Sunday that any French or British warships entering the Strait of Hormuz to accompany U.S. forces would face a "decisive and immediate response" from Iran's armed forces, escalating a standoff over one of the world's most strategically vital waterways.

item.title: Trump calls Iran's response to US peace plan 'totally unacceptable'
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Sunday rejected Iran's reply to the latest American ceasefire proposal, calling it "totally unacceptable" and casting fresh doubt on prospects for ending a war now in its fourth month. The dismissal came hours after Tehran transmitted its formal response through Pakistani mediators, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.

The exchange marks the latest failure in a series of proposals and counterproposals traded between Washington and Tehran since a fragile ceasefire took effect on April 8. Despite weeks of shuttle diplomacy involving Pakistan, Qatar and other intermediaries, the two sides remain far apart on core issues including Iran's nuclear program, the fate of the Strait of Hormuz and the scope of American sanctions relief.

item.title: Second Qatar LNG tanker approaches Hormuz as Pakistan negotiates more shipments
item.description: A Qatari tanker carrying liquefied natural gas crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, marking the first successful LNG transit through the chokepoint since the US-Iran war began on February 28, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. A second vessel, the Mihzem, is now also approaching the strait en route to Pakistan.

item.title: Putin says war 'coming to an end' as Germany rejects his peace mediator
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin told reporters on Saturday that he believes the war in Ukraine is "approaching its end," hours after presiding over the most diminished Victory Day parade in Moscow in nearly two decades — one that for the first time since 2007 featured no tanks, missiles, or other heavy military equipment on Red Square. The remarks, made on May 9 amid a U.S.-brokered three-day ceasefire, drew immediate skepticism from analysts who said they were aimed at a domestic audience rather than reflecting any genuine shift toward peace.

item.title: Iran calls its peace terms 'generous' after Trump rejection
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry pushed back Monday against President Donald Trump's rejection of Tehran's latest counterproposal to end the ten-week war, as oil prices surged and prospects for a diplomatic resolution dimmed further.

item.title: Trump says Iran cease-fire on 'massive life support'
item.description:
President Trump on Monday cast doubt on the survival of the U.S.-Iran cease-fire, saying the agreement was on "massive life support" and had just a "1% chance of living" after he rejected Tehran's latest counterproposal for failing to address its nuclear program.

Speaking alongside Dr. Mehmet Oz at an unrelated White House maternal health event, Trump called the Iranian proposal a "piece of garbage" and said he had not even finished reading it. "I would call it the weakest right now after reading that piece of garbage they sent us," he said during an Oval Office appearance.

item.title: Iran releases Nobel laureate Mohammadi on bail amid health crisis
item.description:
Iranian authorities released Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi on bail on Sunday and transferred her to a Tehran hospital for specialized medical treatment, her foundation announced, following weeks of mounting alarm over her deteriorating health in prison.

The 54-year-old human rights activist had been held at Zanjan prison in northwestern Iran since her arrest on December 12, and her supporters said the transfer came after persistent appeals from her family, legal team, and international figures including the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

item.title: Trump says he may revive Strait of Hormuz operation
item.description:
President Trump said Monday he is considering reviving "Project Freedom," the short-lived U.S. naval escort operation through the Strait of Hormuz, but warned that any renewed effort would go far beyond merely guiding ships and would be "only a piece" of a larger military operation.

The remarks, made in a conversation with Fox News correspondent John Roberts, came after Trump on Sunday rejected Iran's counterproposal to end the roughly ten-week war as "totally unacceptable," posting on Truth Social: "I have just reviewed the reply from Iran's so-called 'Representatives.' I am not pleased — TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!"

item.title: Over 60 Labour MPs call on Starmer to resign as government aides quit
item.description: The rebellion against Prime Minister Keir Starmer escalated sharply on Monday as more than 60 Labour MPs publicly called on him to step down, and four junior members of the government resigned their posts to join the revolt. The growing mutiny, which now spans both the party's left and right flanks, represents the most serious internal threat to a sitting British prime minister in a generation.

item.title: UAE secretly struck Iran's Lavan Island refinery, WSJ reports
item.description: The United Arab Emirates carried out covert military strikes against Iran during the wider U.S.-Israeli war, including an attack on the oil refinery on Iran's Lavan Island on April 8 that triggered a large fire, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday. The revelation confirms weeks of speculation that the Gulf monarchy moved beyond its defensive posture to become a direct, if undeclared, participant in the conflict — a development that Washington quietly welcomed, according to Ynet News.
